_comment: Benchmark constants v3. The reference numbers the build still reads, after the quartile-lever model was retired on 2026-09-23 (docs/DATA_MODEL.md #3): the basket of comparable launches is the benchmark for every volume and rate. What stays: order_split (the medians split a display group's target across its raw channels, since the panel is grouped), cost_per_purchase (the Median is the default price of a paid unit; a release can type its own), the entry-to-order rates, cannibalisation 0.2 (the LE standard per the workbook's spend rules), the framing defaults, the budget sense check, the spend rules and the cost-curve priors. Transcribed from the 2026-08-28 LAUNCH PERFORMANCE OVERVIEW (recomputed panel; quartiles over the historical release panel). See docs/DATA_MODEL.md #4 for provenance. Currency EUR: the spend and the prices these were computed from are Meta's and Shopify's euro figures.

order_split._meaning: channel share of unadjusted draw+preorder units, Low=P25 / Medium=median / High=P75; the build reads the Medium column only, renormalised inside each display group, to split a group's basket target across its channels

cost_per_purchase._meaning: EUR per paid unit, quartiles over the paid campaigns on file; Median is the default the paid budget is priced at when a release has no cost_per_purchase of its own

spend_rules.cpe_daily_drift_note: Prior for the pure time drift in cost per entry, per day, net of spend, the same in every third of the window. Fixed-effect fit on 29 campaigns / 433 campaign-days (etl/analysis/cpe_elasticity.py, 2026-09-23): 2.6% a day +/- 0.5 on calendar days, 2.6-4.0% across day filters and weightings, 1.4% +/- 0.7 on the 2026 campaigns alone, 3.8% before 2026; per-campaign fits spread with a between-campaign sd of 3.4 points a day (cpe_daily_drift_sd). The 2026-09-07 fit on 13 campaigns / 170 days read 0.36% +/- 1.12 and set 0.5%; the wider panel says that was low. The workbook's 5/7/10% a day (kept in cpe_daily_drift_by_third_workbook) is the cost rise along its own ramping spend path, which the elasticity already prices, so it is not applied on top. A campaign with cpe_fit_min_days of history gets its own drift fitted and shrunk to this prior by precision; for most campaigns the prior dominates, because a campaign that ramps spend and ages at the same time cannot tell the two apart from its own days.
spend_rules._source: The cumulative-ROI bands (0.9 / 1.3), the 30% cap and the 10% dead band are the TL template's 'ROI / SPEND RULES - DO NOT CHANGE' block (LAUNCH PERFORMANCE OVERVIEW, TL_Template rows 416-428), applied to LE for want of a fuller LE block. The LE template's own SPEND RULES (rows 284-299) are: decrease/increase steps of 10%, max increase per day 2.0, target ROI AA 1.1, a 30% decrease on a zero-conversion day, a 100% decrease (pause) after 3 days of zero conversion, and 'Expected Increase in Spend (%)' 5/7/10 by third - a typed constant with no derivation, read by row 206 as the daily growth of the forecast cost per unit. Neither tab derives its drift from data; the TL tab labels its 2.16%/day '(assumed)'.

cpe_spend_elasticity_note: Prior for the within-campaign elasticity of cost per entry to daily spend. Fixed-effect fit with a calendar-day drift term on 29 campaigns / 433 campaign-days (etl/analysis/cpe_elasticity.py, 2026-09-23): 0.35-0.45 depending on the day filter (0.377 +/- 0.038 on every day with an entry); the 2026-09-07 fit on 13 campaigns gave 0.384 +/- 0.062. Per-campaign fits spread with a between-campaign sd of 0.19 (cpe_spend_elasticity_sd), which is the prior's width. A campaign with cpe_fit_min_days of history gets its own elasticity fitted and shrunk to this prior by precision (etl/build.py campaign_cost_terms); the prior alone prices a campaign without history. Doubling daily spend raises CPE ~30% at 0.38. Set to 0 to price entries flat.
cpe_growth_factor_note: Superseded: the forward cost per entry now follows spend_rules.cpe_daily_drift_by_third compounded day by day (the path the ROI chart draws), for the budget and the ROI floor alike. Kept for reference only.
